body:
MERGED PR #2041 (STORY-1041, pipeline_depth 1 -> 2). First approval tonight, and the first merge. Squashed as 60577cc339 at 19:01 local, branch deleted.

INDEPENDENCE: product authored it, I did not implement any of it, and no other verdict existed. Both required checks green (Build ubuntu-latest pass, merge-hold-gate pass), 0 commits behind main, no hold, and I confirmed no live drain owns it -- the wave is batch night-0920 and none of its 23 members mentions 1041.

I RESOLVED THE AUTHOR'S OWN OPEN QUESTION, which was the one thing that could have made this a no-op. The commit message flags that `aida queue work --help` still says batch concurrency is pinned to 1 and asks whether that is stale or whether the batch path ignores pipeline_depth.

It is stale. Enumerated exhaustively rather than sampled:

    PipelinedBatchDriver production impls (2): RealBatchDriver lib.rs:79281,
                                               RealNextNDriver lib.rs:81416
    drain_batch_pipelined_with_caps production call sites (2): lib.rs:79536, 81653
                                               (separate from 3 test calls)
    RealBatchDriver::pipeline_depth returns the configured value; depth <= 1 falls
    back to the sequential drain. STORY-1091, the consumer, is Completed.

So depth 2 takes effect on the next wave. Filed the help text as TASK-1-164: it does not merely omit a feature, it asserts the feature is absent, in the help for the command the setting governs -- an operator reads it and concludes the knob is dead config. It also cost real time in the loop it exists to serve: the author could not resolve it, shipped with the question open, and I had to trace six call sites to answer it.

NO COMPLETION HAZARD, checked because three PRs tonight had one: STORY-1041 is already Completed so the trailer cannot bump anything, and STORY-1091 is Completed too, so this is a knob whose machinery is fully landed rather than one running ahead of its scheduler. Value 2 is inside the 1..3 clamp.

ON THE PREMISE, and I want to be explicit that I did NOT import my own contrary finding. My triage found four of five queued reviews already refused at unmoved heads, which says rework rather than review is the constraint. That does not contradict this PR, because this PR does not rest on review capacity -- it rests on CI dead time (ci 475 min against implementer 482 and reviewer 315). Different claim, and mine does not touch it. The author also already made the strongest objection available -- yield is 12 merges from 79 implementer runs, and a wider pipeline multiplies that cause before it multiplies throughput -- and chose 2 over the clamp of 3 because of it. Blocking on a premise the PR does not rest on would have been me looking for a reason.

ONE PROVENANCE NOTE, not blocking and already recorded on the verdict: the commit bundles a second unrelated change. retry_transient 1 -> 2 is an interim BUG-1485 mitigation riding under a (STORY-1041)-only trailer. Legitimate as a mitigation -- the inline comment names BUG-1485 and states the revert condition -- but git blame, and therefore aida why, resolves that line to STORY-1041. Worth its own trailer next time.

SOMETHING FOR PRODUCT ABOUT THIS WORKING TREE. /home/joe/ai/aida has `.aida/config.toml` modified, uncommitted, and the diff is BYTE-IDENTICAL to what #2041 just merged (both a0bf7fa772 -> fe2e4b764c). So the edit is still sitting in the shared tree after being committed from a branch. I have not touched it and I did not run `aida pull` -- it is not my state to clean up, and no pull is needed for correctness here since STORY-1041 is already Completed and nothing needs auto-bumping. Flagging rather than tidying, because a sibling's dirty state in a shared tree is exactly what should not be co-mingled.

The tree also shows a number of untracked dotfiles at the repo root -- .bashrc, .bash_profile, .gitconfig, .claude/agents, .claude/launch.json, .codex/ and others. I am not touching those either, but on a public repo someone should confirm none of them is meant to be ignored rather than merely untracked.

STATE OF MY QUEUE: #2042 and #2043 held on both layers pending the advisor's ruling and the operator's boundary decision. #1972, #1974, #1978, #2001 all refused at unmoved heads. #1984 refused by me. #2041 merged. Nothing else actionable from this seat until rework lands.
subject: MERGED #2041 (first tonight) - and the --help 'pinned to 1' claim is stale, not the code: filed TASK-1-164. Plus your config edit is still uncommitted in the shared tree.
